outcome: Perceived Interpersonal Relevancy Scales (PIRS) factor structure and internal consistency
cohort: The study included 1,079 adults aged 18-90 years recruited online from the general population of Australia.
finding: The study successfully developed and validated the Perceived Interpersonal Relevancy Scales (PIRS), demonstrating its factor structure and internal consistency, and found that higher self-perceived threat and invisibility were associated with decreased social network size, increased loneliness, younger age, and male sex, while higher opportunity was linked to increased social network size and decreased loneliness.
